Oh boy, where should I start? Alright, let me try.

It was is a fantastic game. It is one of the first game **games** that I've been able to play on this crappy computer, and boy was I glad it could. This game is probably the best, even now, 11 years later.

*GAMEPLAY*

It is very fun, period. The mechanics like gravity gun make it very exciting, and the game itself is very fast paced. Sometimes, it can even be quite scary, with dark places like ravenholm. The physics are solid, the controls are solid, and so it everything else.

10/10 on gameplay.

*GRAPHICS*

Now, I can't say that its a bad game because of this. It's 11 year old game, up close textures look quite blurry (like console, HUEHUHE AMIRITE?!) but when not up close, it actually looks quite amazing, and very VERY immersive. It seems to be very optimised too, I can only dream of a game looking like this run at 60 FPS on this piece of crap.

9/10 on graphics.

*STORY*

Very immersive. Nuff said.

3333333333/10

Half-Life 2 is still an awesome game even though it's an older game. Valve updated the game's graphics. The graphics do look much better now. There are all kinds of creatures and characters to interact with. I recommend buying The Orange Box if you want Half-Life 2 with the updated graphics and new episodes. There have been many mods for Half-Life 2. Most of them were never finished, or they quit working after Valve made updates to the Source game engine. One of the best mods I played was Deep Down. It's on the MODDB website. Valve never made Half-Life 2: Episode 3. I would play Deep Down or The Closure if you want something like an Episode 3 for the game. I would install Mapbase too. Mapbase will improve the graphics for HL2 mods. There are a few other good mods like Nightmare House 2, Spherical Nightmares, Rabbit Hole, Riot Act, and Snowdrop Escape. Be sure to put "+mat_queue_mode -1" without the quotes into the Steam launch options. That command should improve the performance of any Steam game. I recently learned that Half-Life 2 has mods and maps available on the Steam Workshop now. It's hard to believe people are still creating mods for a game that will be more than twenty years old soon.

Half-Life 2 (HL2) is a story driven first person shooter (fps) game. The physics-centred game engine plays a central role in both puzzle solving and combat, as one of the main weapons (Gravity Gun) allows to pull in objects to then launch them back again at enemies or structures. The game starts with your mysterious arrival in City 17 and as you proceed, the story is told through scripted in-game scenes while the player retains full control over the main protagonist.

Released more than 20 years ago, HL2 is often considered one of the best fps games ever made and genre-defining for story telling in fps games. In November 2024 Valve updated HL2 with graphical enhancements, quality of life features and integrated both sequels "HL2 Episode 1" and "HL2 Episode 2" into HL2. These enhancements are appreciated as those of the original fan base, who have not yet died of old age, still eagerly await Half-Life 3 ...
In my opinion, one of the most interesting and addictive FPS games ever. Learn the story (not necessarily by playing HL) and play this game and it's two chronological episodes.

Review:
As someone who has heard a lot of fanfare about Half Life but never played it; it is surprising to find that this game has not only delivered, but rather also stood the test of time. Story keeps you wondering and yet on the edge of your seat. Audio is queued for maximum scenario realism/adrenaline rushes. Visuals talk much about the age of the game but the dynamics of the visuals compare to some modern games.

Rants:
Bit annoyed at the ending as it made little sense what you had to do to get to the end.
Liniarity of the game helped steer the story but some bits were not as clear as they should have been. Dang striders.

Bottom Line: If you havent played this game yet. Go do so. Its worth the ruckus its fanbase has made. Get ready to get back into that HEV suit and swing that crowbar! The Freeman is here!
If its too old looking try the Update version.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (97%): players mostly praise the story and characters.

details.text: Complaints about bugs and crashes have fallen sharply in the last 30 days, so recent buyers are less likely to run into them.
Players with fewer hours are a little less positive, at 93% against 99% for those with the most hours.
